idiom_name: Codable message struct plus extension init(_ order:)/var message; JSONEncoder at the endpoint
implementation_notes: The message is a dedicated struct OrderMessage: Codable and the mapper is an extension next to it - extension OrderMessage { init(_ order: Order) } plus a factory on the domain side - invoked by the producer/consumer (a SwiftNIO/Vapor queue handler or an AsyncSequence of messages). Codable's synthesised conformance and JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder cover the wire half (CodingKeys for wire names, keyDecodingStrategy for blanket conventions), while flattening the aggregate (customer to customerId, money to minor units, identity resolution on the way in) stays in the initialiser; the classic mapper object collapses into that extension. Unlike the pure format-translation case, Codable does not absorb the domain mapping, so the pattern remains an explicit local idiom rather than native syntax.
pitfalls: Declaring init(_:) or init(from:) in the type's main declaration removes the memberwise initialiser; put the mapper initialiser in an extension so the message keeps it.
Codable synthesis changes silently when a stored property type stops being codable or a CodingKeys case is added: pin the wire contract with golden-payload tests.
Value semantics copy on assignment: mapping a large collection allocates a full copy per element unless the mapping is streamed.
JSONDecoder.keyDecodingStrategy is global to the decoder: converting snake_case for one message type changes every model decoded by that instance.
